Mutate the supplied array in place; return no value. The full multiset must be preserved.

examples.explanation: For k=2 and [4,7,9], one possible pair of draws chooses 9 first and 4 second, leaving sample prefix [9,4]. The possible subsets {4,7}, {4,9} and {7,9} each have probability 1/3. online_sampling.description: Select a uniform random k-element subset of positions from a finite stream, using one pass and a reservoir. Return the sampled values in any order; do not select a stream position twice.
constraints: 0≤k≤stream length. Values are integers; the statistical wrapper uses distinct values.

nonuniform_random_number.description: Given corresponding values and probabilities, return one random value with its specified probability. Repeated calls must implement the requested distribution.
constraints: The two nonempty lists have equal length; probabilities are finite, nonnegative and sum to 1. Values are distinct in the distribution checker.
Return a single supplied value without changing either list. Probability-zero values must not be selected in the ideal interval model.

examples.explanation: For values [4,9] with probabilities [0.25,0.75], draws below 0.25 return 4 and draws from 0.25 onward return 9. A draw of 0.6 therefore returns 9; repeated draws select 9 three times as often on average. JSON arguments are [values,probabilities]. Observed true validates repeated samples; the callable returns one value. Finite samples do not prove exact randomness.

constraints: For a nonempty grid, n rows each have n entries, n is a perfect square, and entries lie in 0…n. Regions have side √n.

bst_from_sorted_array.description: Build a BST of minimum height whose inorder traversal equals the supplied sorted array, preserving every occurrence. Return its root. Height counts nodes, so an empty tree has height zero.
constraints: Input is a nondecreasing integer array, possibly empty. Duplicate keys may appear on either side under the inclusive BST convention.
Allocate new nodes without changing the input. Any minimum-height structure with the required inorder contents is valid; the wrapper returns its checked height.
An empty input returns a null root; the displayed solutions choose the upper middle for an even-sized range.

adding_credits.description: Implement a client-credit database. Insert replaces a client’s credit; Remove reports whether it existed; Lookup returns its credit or −1; AddAll adds an amount to every current client; Max returns any client ID with greatest credit, or an empty string when empty.
constraints: Client IDs are nonempty strings. Credits and increments are integers; observed credits must fit the public result type. Operations may include negative increments.

Maintain state across operations on one instance. Reinitialization or a new instance resets the database. Any tied maximum ID is acceptable. The judge maintains expected credits independently and accepts any existing client with the maximum credit. No universal tie-breaker is required.
Removing a missing client returns false; reinserting sets an absolute credit, independent of prior AddAll calls.

examples.explanation: Insert client Nora with credit 4, then AddAll(6): Lookup(Nora) is 10. Reinsert Nora with credit 3, which replaces its absolute credit. Max is Nora; after removal Lookup is −1 and Max is empty. JSON arguments are [operations], with each operation [name,stringArg,intArg]. lookup/remove/max records carry expected observations, not extra callable parameters. Observed true means all operations validated.

constraints: Input is a finite binary tree, possibly empty; data values do not affect balance.

tree_right_sibling.description: Set each node’s Next link to the node immediately to its right on the same level, or null for the last node of that level.
constraints: Input is a perfect binary tree: all internal nodes have two children and all leaves share a depth. Initial Next links are null; an empty tree is allowed.
Mutate only Next links; retain every node, data value and child link. The callable returns no value; the wrapper displays the verified level chains.
The root and each level’s last node point to null; singleton and empty trees need no child links.

examples.explanation: For perfect tree [16, 7, 25, 2, 11, 20, 30], set root Next to null. Link 7 → 25 → null. On the leaf level, sibling links give 2 → 11 and 20 → 30, while the cross-parent link gives 11 → 20. The complete chain is 2 → 11 → 20 → 30 → null. The adapter returns the verified levels [[16], [7, 25], [2, 11, 20, 30]]. JSON arguments are [tree]. Observed output is the verified list of levels reached by Next links; the callable itself returns void/None.

knapsack.description: Choose a subset of items maximizing total value while total weight is at most capacity. Each item may be selected at most once; return the best value.
constraints: Each item is (weight,value), in that order. Weights and capacity are nonnegative integers; values are integers. The empty selection is allowed. Numeric totals must fit the selected type.

Capacity zero can still admit zero-weight items. Empty items return zero; a heavier item cannot be chosen.

examples.explanation: For items (weight,value) [(2,7),(3,9),(4,12)] and capacity 5, choosing the first two gives weight 5 and value 16. The last item alone gives only 12, so the answer remains 16. is_string_decomposable_into_words.description: Split the entire input string into dictionary words, preserving character order. Return any valid sequence of words, or an empty list if no decomposition exists. A dictionary word may be reused.
constraints: Input string may be empty; dictionary entries are nonempty strings, compared exactly using the language’s string semantics.
Return a new word list without changing the dictionary. Concatenating a successful result must reproduce the entire input. The empty string has the empty decomposition.
Multiple decompositions are accepted; a matching prefix without a matching remainder is insufficient.

examples.explanation: For "sunleaf" and {"sun","leaf","sunl"}, prefix "sun" becomes reachable at 3 and "sunl" at 4. Only the split after 3 can finish with dictionary word "leaf", so reconstruct ["sun","leaf"]. JSON arguments are [domain,dictionary,canDecompose]. The last Boolean belongs only to the validator. The callable takes the first two arguments and returns words; observed true means that output satisfied the feasibility oracle.

search_maze.description: Find any path through white maze cells from start to end, moving only horizontally or vertically. Include both endpoints. Return an empty path if no path exists; a shortest path is not required.
constraints: The maze uses 0 for white/passable and 1 for black/blocked. Coordinates are (row,column), zero-based. Selected endpoints are cells in the maze.
Return a coordinate list. C#/JavaScript preserve the maze; C++ searches a copy; Python/Java mark visited cells in the supplied maze. The wrapper validates the path against the original maze.
A white start equal to end returns a one-cell path. Blocked or unreachable endpoints yield an empty path.

examples.explanation: For maze [[0,0,1],[1,0,0],[0,0,0]], start (0,0) and end (2,2), BFS can discover (0,0)→(0,1)→(1,1)→(2,1)→(2,2). Every step is orthogonal and every visited cell is white, so return that path; the judge validates it as true. JSON arguments are [maze,[startRow,startColumn],[endRow,endColumn]]. Observed true means a valid path was accepted; observed false for distinct unreachable endpoints corresponds to an empty returned path. The wrapper also observes true for any empty result when start=end, a weaker check than the callable’s path contract.

checks.actualAlgorithm: For each of the first k positions, uniformly choose one still-unselected entry and swap it into place. This partial Fisher–Yates shuffle preserves the full multiset and makes every k-element subset equally likely.
checks.correctness: At position i, every still-unselected entry has equal chance of being chosen from the remaining suffix. Thus every ordered k-tuple of distinct entries has probability 1/(n·(n−1)···(n−k+1)), and summing over its k! orders makes every k-element subset equally likely. Swaps preserve the full multiset.
checks.workedTrace: For k=2 and [4,7,9], one possible pair of draws chooses 9 first and 4 second, leaving sample prefix [9,4]. The possible subsets {4,7}, {4,9} and {7,9} each have probability 1/3. JSON arguments are [k,A]. The observed true is statistical validation of repeated mutated prefixes, not the callable return.
checks.edgeCases: k=0 chooses the empty subset. k equal to the length chooses all entries. Entries outside the sampled prefix remain part of the preserved full multiset.
checks.timeDerivation: O(k). There are exactly k constant-sized swaps and only loop indices beyond the input.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1). Only two indices and a swap temporary are retained; the input array is reused.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Fill a reservoir with the first k entries. For the entry at zero-based index i, choose a random position among i+1 possibilities and replace a reservoir slot only when that position is below k. This preserves equal probability for every k-element subset.
checks.correctness: After t entries, every k-subset has probability 1/C(t,k). Initially t=k and there is only one subset. At the next entry, an old subset survives when no slot is replaced, with probability (t+1−k)/(t+1). A desired subset containing the new entry has t+1−k possible predecessor subsets; each selects the slot of its one extra old entry with probability 1/(t+1). Both cases therefore have probability 1/C(t+1,k), proving uniformity of complete subsets, not merely equal individual inclusion probabilities.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Breadth-first search the starting cell’s same-color component. Flip a cell when it is enqueued so it cannot be enqueued twice, and explore only horizontal and vertical neighbors of its original color.
checks.correctness: Only cells matching the starting original color are enqueued, and each is flipped before enqueuing. That flip marks it visited, so no cell is processed twice. Four-neighbor expansion reaches exactly the starting component and changes no differently colored or disconnected cell.
checks.workedTrace: For start (0,0) in [[1,1,0],[0,1,0],[1,0,0]], the connected 1 cells are (0,0),(0,1),(1,1). Flipping them gives [[0,0,0],[0,0,0],[1,0,0]]; the isolated 1 at (2,0) remains. JSON arguments are [row,column,image], not [image,row,column]. The observed output is the mutated image; native Boolean image types are converted by their wrappers.
checks.edgeCases: Diagonal contact alone does not connect cells. An isolated starting pixel is still flipped. The starting value determines the component before any recoloring.
checks.timeDerivation: O(rows × columns). Each component cell is flipped before enqueueing and considers four neighbors, preventing duplicate enqueues.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(rows × columns). The queue contains cells from the component; JavaScript retains its consumed queue entries until the call ends.

The observed output is the mutated image; native Boolean image types are converted by their wrappers.
